messages.content: What is the best month to visit Hawaii?

message.content:
The “best” month to visit Hawaii really depends on what you’re looking for—weather, crowds, or price—but most travelers agree that **late spring (April–May) and early fall (September–October)** strike the best balance.

| What you care about | Why those months work |
|---------------------|-----------------------|
| **Weather** | Average highs hover around 80 °F (27 °C) and lows stay above 65 °F (18 °C). It’s warm enough for beach fun but not as hot or humid as the peak summer months. |
| **Crowds** | These periods sit just outside the high‑season rush (June–August). You’ll find fewer tourists, shorter lines at popular sights, and a more relaxed vibe. |
| **Prices** | Hotels and flights often drop after the summer peak, so you can snag better rates while still enjoying great weather. |
| **Events** | Late spring and early fall host a variety of cultural festivals and local celebrations, giving you a taste of Hawaiian life beyond the beaches. |

### Quick Weather Snapshot (average temperatures)

| Month | Avg. High | Avg. Low |
|-------|-----------|----------|
| April | ~80 °F (27 °C) | ~65 °F (18 °C) |
| May | ~81 °F (27 °C) | ~66 °F (19 °C) |
| September | ~82 °F (28 °C) | ~67 °F (19 °C) |
| October | ~81 °F (27 °C) | ~66 °F (19 °C) |

*(These figures come from NOAA’s climate normals for Honolulu.)*

---

#### Bottom line
If you want pleasant weather, fewer crowds, and better deals, aim for **April, May, September, or October**. If you’re okay with higher prices and don’t mind the heat, the summer months (June–August) still offer fantastic beach days and vibrant nightlife. Happy planning!
